top10.introHtml: Ranked across 55 filtered listings from Cars.com (14), CarGurus (22), and AutoTrader (19). TrueCar skipped — body-style filter broken. Seat filter applied: excluded all 2-seat roadsters (Miata, S2000, Solstice, Boxster, Z3/Z4, TT Roadster, Thunderbird, SC 430, Allante, smart ForTwo, etc.). Personal excludes applied: MINI, Buick, Camry Solara, Camaro, Volvo, Mustang pre-2005. No manual-transmission convertibles surfaced this refresh — manual10 is empty. Image coverage: Cars.com 100% (14/14), CarGurus 100% (22/22), AutoTrader 100% (19/19).

picks.whyGood: Literally 2 miles from Media — walk there to look at it. The CLK 350's M272 V6 is one of Mercedes' most reliable engines, 65k miles is low for a 2009, and the 4-seat cabriolet body is elegant without being fussy. Prime Autohaus is a local independent with strong reviews. Fair Deal from CarGurus means the price is market-accurate.
picks.whatToVerify: Full convertible-top cycle (open and close with engine running), check headliner and rear carpet for water stains from top seal, check rocker panels for rust bubbling, inspect soft-top fabric for tears/delamination at the rear window seam. CLK-specific: listen for timing chain rattle on cold start, check for oil leaks at valve cover and rear main.
picks.bottomLine: Best location in the pool at 2 miles, low miles, bulletproof engine — start here.

picks.whyGood: 48k miles on a BMW 135i is extraordinary — this engine likely hasn't been pushed hard. The N54 twin-turbo makes 300hp and sounds fantastic. The 1-Series convertible has a proper back seat (tight but real), making it a genuine 4-seater. At under 50k miles, most consumables are still healthy. Strong candidate for the most fun per dollar in this pool.
picks.whatToVerify: N54 known issues: high-pressure fuel pump (HPFP) failure — confirm no hesitation at light throttle, check for wastegate rattle on cold start, look for injector tick. Full top cycle, rear-window seam, soft-top motor function. Oil leaks at valve cover. Ask for service history — timing chain stretch is possible if intervals were skipped.
picks.bottomLine: 48k miles on a twin-turbo BMW 135i is the find of this refresh — inspect carefully and snap it up.

picks.whyGood: 4 miles from Media and a 2016 model — the newest Audi in the pool. The A3 Cabriolet is a proper 4-seat drop-top with a proven 2.0T engine and DSG/S-tronic gearbox. Private seller through PSE means you can negotiate and inspect without dealer pressure. 84k miles is moderate and the 2.0 EA888 engine is durable with proper maintenance.
picks.whatToVerify: Full top cycle (the A3 cabriolet cloth top is generally trouble-free), check drain channels under the top frame for debris. EA888 engine: look for oil consumption, water pump and thermostat history, carbon buildup on intake valves (walnut blast if none done). DSG/S-tronic: confirm smooth shifts, no shudder at low speed. Check CarFax for any gap in service records.
picks.bottomLine: Four miles away, 2016 model, private seller — the most modern and practical choice close to home.

picks.whyGood: The newest car in the entire pool — a 2020 S550 Mustang EcoBoost. Fred Beans is a reputable Ford franchise dealer, likely CPO-inspected. The 2.3T EcoBoost is well proven by 2020 and handles 130k+ miles routinely with oil changes. The S550 convertible top is far more reliable than older designs. You get modern safety tech, SYNC infotainment, and a proper folding soft-top.
picks.whatToVerify: S550 2020: check for rear camera function, top seals around the rear quarter window, water staining on rear seat fabric. Confirm no cam-phaser noise (a minor S550 gripe). EcoBoost: check for turbo boost leaks, intercooler hose clamps. At 132k request full service record from Fred Beans — they may have records in their system.
picks.bottomLine: Newest car in the pool from a name-brand dealer — the safest buy if 132k miles doesn't scare you.

picks.whyGood: Being sold at a Lexus dealer means it passed their inspection threshold. The 2016 S550 EcoBoost has 106k miles — lighter use than the 2020 above. Fair Deal per CarGurus. 14 miles from Media is very manageable. The S550 generation is a huge step up from the S197 in refinement and convertible-top quality.
picks.whatToVerify: Same S550 checks as rank 4. The Lexus dealer inspection is a positive signal, but get your own PPI. Ask for the CarFax — confirm one or two owners and no fleet use. Check the top seal at the rear quarter for any cracking; the 2015-17 S550 tops occasionally show early wear there.
picks.bottomLine: Inspected by a luxury dealer, 14 miles away — solid alternative to the 2020 at a slight price premium.

picks.whyGood: The E46 330Ci is widely regarded as one of the best driver's BMWs ever made. The naturally aspirated M54 inline-6 has a stellar reliability record — no turbo complexity, just smooth linear power. 84k miles is modest and the E46 4-seat cabriolet is a proven, beloved design. Under $10k for this combination is excellent value.
picks.whatToVerify: E46 specific: check rear subframe mounting points for cracking (known E46 issue — look underneath with a light). Top hydraulic rams — open and close fully, listen for pump whine. Check for coolant system health (plastic coolant expansion tanks crack). Oil leaks at VANOS unit and valve cover are common. Rear-window rear-seat water staining.
picks.bottomLine: The legendary E46 at under $10k — inspect the subframe and top rams, then drive it home.

picks.whyGood: The E93 335i convertible is the turbocharged step up from the 328/330 — more power, same 4-seat layout. 94k is reasonable on the N54 engine if maintained. At $9,999 from CarVision (an established dealer) it's priced at Fair Deal. Only 16 miles from Media. If you want more performance than the 330Ci at rank 6, this is your car.
picks.whatToVerify: N54 same as rank 2: HPFP, wastegate rattle, injector tick. E93-specific: the convertible top hydraulic pump is under the trunk floor — confirm no error codes, full cycle smooth and quiet. Check rocker panels for rust. Oil cooler seal is another N54 maintenance item to confirm.
picks.bottomLine: Twin-turbo power at 16 miles out and under $10k — the sporty buy in this tier.

picks.whyGood: A 2015 BMW 435i xDrive Cabriolet for $8,500 is a genuinely good deal by any measure — these list for $15k+ when clean. xDrive AWD is a bonus in PA/NJ winters. The F33 generation is a big refinement over the E93. The N55 single-turbo inline-6 is more reliable than the N54 in the 335i. 140k is higher but the value is hard to argue with.
picks.whatToVerify: Private seller — PPI is mandatory. N55 engine: check for oil leaks (common at valve cover, oil filter housing), coolant hose condition. F33 convertible top: confirm fully waterproof, no sagging headliner, drain channels clear. xDrive transfer case fluid — ask for service history. At 140k the cooling system may be overdue for refresh.
picks.bottomLine: Best dollars-per-car ratio in the pool — private seller means PPI is essential but the upside is real.

picks.whyGood: The most powerful car in the pool. The B8 S5 Cabriolet with the 3.0T supercharged V6 makes 333hp, sounds incredible, and quattro AWD is always on. 69k miles is relatively low. Clean title and no accidents on Cars.com. At $13,642 it's not cheap but it's the sporty-luxury pick. Prestige trim means all options included.
picks.whatToVerify: S5 3.0T supercharger: confirm no whining or belt slip. Carbon buildup on intake valves (direct injection) — ask if walnut-blasted. Audi S5 specific: check torque converter shudder (7-speed S-tronic), timing chain tensioner condition, thermostat housing (plastic, cracks). Convertible top: full cycle test, check drain channels, rear window seam. At this price expect an independent Audi PPI.
picks.bottomLine: Most powerful and prestigious car in the pool — budget $500-1000 for PPI and maintenance items at Royal Auto.

picks.whyGood: 34,866 miles on a 2001 CLK 430 is genuinely remarkable — this engine has barely been broken in. The M113 4.3L V8 is one of the most reliable Mercedes engines ever produced. 22 miles from Media at a local dealer (Selden Motors in Willow Grove). The CLK 430 Cabriolet is a proper 4-seat cruiser with real V8 character. Rare find at this mileage.
picks.whatToVerify: At 25 years old with low miles, check for rubber degradation more than mechanical wear: top seals, all hoses, fuel injector seals, brake lines. Confirm the car has been stored properly — low-mile classics can have issues from sitting. Top cycle full test. M113: confirm no crankshaft position sensor codes, check for cam adjuster noise. Independent PPI mandatory.
picks.bottomLine: 34k miles on a V8 Mercedes CLK is a unicorn — verify storage history, then decide.

manual10.introHtml: No manual-transmission convertibles surfaced in this refresh across all three sources. All 55 filtered listings are either automatic or transmission-unknown (CarGurus and AutoTrader listings rarely expose transmission in their SRP data). If a manual is important, consider checking individual VDP pages for promising stick-shift candidates like the BMW 330Ci, 335i, or Audi S5 — those trims were available with 6-speed manuals.

mustangs.introHtml: Three unique 2005+ Mustang convertibles found in the 35-mile radius at this price point: a 2020 EcoBoost Premium (Fred Beans Langhorne), a 2016 EcoBoost Premium (Lexus of Wilmington), and a 2014 V6 (Josie's Auto Sales). No GT or Shelby variants appeared in budget. All are S550 or late S197 generation — no Fox-body or early SN-95 cars in range.

picks.whyGood: Newest Mustang in the pool by 4 years; S550 EcoBoost is proven at high miles. Fred Beans franchise dealer inspection.
picks.whatToVerify: Top seals at rear quarter, rear camera, confirm no cam-phaser noise, full service record from dealer.
picks.bottomLine: Best Mustang in the pool — newest generation from a reputable dealer.

picks.whyGood: Inspected at a luxury dealer, 14 miles from Media, 106k miles is lighter use. Fair Deal CarGurus rating.
picks.whatToVerify: S550 top seal rear quarter, CarFax for owner count, confirm no fleet use.
picks.bottomLine: Closer and lower miles — the tighter find if you can afford the extra $1k.

picks.whyGood: S197 V6 at $9,900 is the budget Mustang option. The 3.7L V6 is reliable to 150k+. Josie's is a repeat dealer in this pool.
picks.whatToVerify: S197 spring perch rust, top latch wear, 8.8 axle clunk on takeoff, rear seat water staining. Confirm top operates without hesitation.
picks.bottomLine: Best-value Mustang — V6 won't thrill but the S197 top and chassis are solid.
